narrative.overview:
The calculator reads like a carefully kept notebook: warm off-white paper, graphite and pencil-grey text, hairline ruled lines, and one hand-drawn curve that carries nearly all of the color. Each period is a different ink on that curve. Everything around the chart is calm, precise and unshowy. It is there to record the plan and report the numbers, never to compete with them.

Density is moderate and work-focused. A fixed-width column on the left holds the plan, written as a timeline: a ruled spine with each period hanging off a numbered node in its own ink. The results column on the right puts the final amount first, then a ruled row of three supporting figures (paid in, growth, monthly income), the chart with each period's stretch labeled above it, and the ledger-style breakdown. Type pairs a serif for the answers (figures and headings, like ink in a ledger) with a quiet sans for the working parts, on a role scale of eight sizes. The one large number on the page is the final amount.

Dark mode is the same notebook read by lamplight: the same roles and the same hues, re-stepped for a near-black page. It is never a separate look.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral paper surfaces; color is reserved for data and the single action accent.
The plan reads as a sequence: a timeline spine down the setup column, labeled stretches on the chart.
Color encodes *which period*; shape encodes *which extra*. Neither channel is borrowed for decoration.
Soft-edged, quiet controls with hairline borders and almost no shadow.
Serif figures with tabular numerals wherever money answers the question.
One display-size number per screen: the final amount.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Hue on the chart, legend, swatches and table dots means *which period* and nothing else. Extras are told apart by shape (circle, square, triangle, diamond) drawn in neutral pencil tones, never by a palette color.

rules.name: The Palette Lives in JS Rule
rules.body: No series hex is ever written in `styles.css` or markup. Every series color is read through `Chart.colorFor(slot)`, and periods store a slot index, never a hex.

rules.name: The Readable Ink Rule
rules.body: A figure set on a series fill (the period node number) takes white or graphite per slot, whichever contrasts more, via `Chart.inkOn(slot)`. Never hardcode white on a palette hue: yellow, aqua and magenta fail with it.

rules.name: The Ink Is for Data Rule
rules.body: Outside the chart and its keys, the only saturated color is Ledger Blue on the primary action and focus. Gain and loss colors tint text only.

rules.name: The Ledger Ink Rule
rules.body: Money that answers the user's question (final amount, summary figures, result bar, tooltip balance) is set in the serif with lining tabular numerals. Money in the table and the inputs stays in the sans: those are working figures, not answers.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every money, percentage or time figure that sits near another figure uses tabular numerals: inputs, figures, table cells, tooltips, axis labels. Free-text inputs turn it back off.

rules.name: The One Big Number Rule
rules.body: Only the final amount is set at display size. If another figure seems to need it, it belongs in the summary row at figure size.

rules.name: The Today's Money Rule
rules.body: Amounts are shown in today's dollars by default (2.5% inflation, editable), with a Today's $ / Future $ switch beside the final amount. The math stays nominal; `Calc.inTodaysDollars` restates a projection so every figure, the chart and the table move together, and the accounting still reconciles. Growth in today's dollars is labeled "Growth after inflation".

rules.name: The No Green Shortfall Rule
rules.body: Once the balance goes below zero, the plan is short: the final amount turns Loss Red under "Shortfall at the end", a Loss Red warning names the month the money runs out, the chart marks it, and nothing about that plan's growth is tinted green.

rules.name: The Whole Dollars Rule
rules.body: Projections are estimates, so every figure on screen rounds to whole dollars. Cents imply a precision the model does not have.

rules.name: The Role Token Rule
rules.body: A new text element picks one of the nine `--text-*` roles. If none fits, the role list changes in DESIGN.md first; no one-off sizes.

rules.name: The Paper Doesn't Float Rule
rules.body: Cards inside a panel (period cards, extra cards) never get a shadow; a hairline border and a tonal step are enough. Shadow is for the panels and for anything that overlays content (tooltip, toast, result bar), and nothing else.

rules.name: The No Card in a Card Rule
rules.body: Inside the results panel, summary figures sit in a ruled row, not in boxes. A new grouping inside a panel uses hairline rules or spacing before it uses a border box.

dos: **Do** read every series color through `Chart.colorFor(slot)` and store a slot index on the data.
**Do** distinguish extras by shape glyph in neutral pencil tones.
**Do** use tabular figures on every number that sits near another number.
**Do** separate layers with a tonal step plus a 1px Ruled Line border before reaching for a shadow.
**Do** keep uppercase labels in Pencil at 12px, 600, with 0.06em tracking.
**Do** set sizes with the `--text-*` role tokens only.
**Do** define every new neutral as a token in both the light `:root` block and the `[data-theme="dark"]` block.
**Do** draw icons as inline SVG at one stroke weight (1.6 at 14px).
**Do** make destructive actions undoable with the toast rather than gating them behind a dialog.
**Do** round on-screen money to whole dollars.
donts: **Don't** hardcode a series hex in `styles.css` or markup, or use a palette hue for anything other than a period.
**Don't** give extras a color of their own.
**Don't** set a second figure at display size; only the final amount is 46px.
**Don't** add a third font family, or load the fonts from a CDN; they ship in `fonts/`.
**Don't** put shadows on cards nested inside a panel, or any shadow in dark mode.
**Don't** use Gain Green or Loss Red as background fills; they tint text and borders only.
**Don't** add a second accent color for interface chrome. Ledger Blue is the only action color.
**Don't** mark a card with a thick colored edge; a period's color lives on its timeline node.
**Don't** use unicode glyphs or emoji as icons, or the native `confirm()` dialog.
**Don't** box figures inside a panel; use a ruled row.
